results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA § 2.2: automatic successive five-year Renewal Terms, notice 'not more than 270 days and not less than 240 days' before expiry. It calls this effectively a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Issue 4 identifies § 3.1's worldwide exclusivity over all glass and PET containers for any beverage product. It contrasts this with the Term Sheet scope of amber glass for beer brands at U.S./Canadian facilities and states that Harrowgate is bound by the executed text.

Issue 1 notes Recital C records receipt on August 3, 2026 and that the window closed September 2, 2026, before the September 21 Amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted and seeks an extension or waiver.

Issue 2 explains Amendment § 2 replaces § 11.2, deletes the Recall carve-out and limits the indemnity carve-out to § 9.1(c) third-party IP claims. It states recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

Issue 5 describes new § 14.4 allowing Supplier to assign without consent to Affiliates or successors, notwithstanding § 14.3. It flags that there is no competitor exclusion and that the restriction is one-sided because Harrowgate still needs consent.
Part I states that under SA § 15.2 written amendments rank above the SA, so the Amendment controls where it conflicts with the SA.
Issue 2 states that § 11.1 caps liability at 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner and organizes issues item by item. Each item has a Location line and a Recommended fix.
The memo proposes specific language for every issue, including a restored § 11.2, a replacement § 3.1, a revised § 2.2 and a competitor exclusion in § 14.4.
The memo states the objection window closed and that Harrowgate cannot now serve a timely objection without an extension.
The memo states that the executed text controls, not the Term Sheet.
